page: Microsoft Azure M256lds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture and powered by dedicated Intel processors. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 256 dedicated virtual CPUs coupled with 3892.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 15.2 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is not present, with zero physical or virtual GPUs configured.

The instance includes 9449 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, providing high-capacity, low-latency scratch space alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. Network interfaces do not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring standard cloud networking allocation for external routing.

In terms of resource allocation and cost efficiency, M256lds_v4 consolidates extreme compute density, terabyte-scale memory, and substantial local NVMe storage onto a single dedicated node. The primary tradeoff centers on the massive scale of the instance, where workloads that cannot fully leverage 256 threads or the 3.8 TB memory footprint will incur unutilized hardware overhead.

This server type is engineered for heavy, memory-intensive enterprise environments. It is suited for large-scale in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, massive relational database management systems, extensive online transaction processing (OLTP), large in-memory caching layers, and high-throughput data analytics pipelines requiring rapid local disk access.
